zh: 给你一个具体的例子，对吧，假设你在某个 EC2 实例上有一个漏洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the biggest challenges that enterprises face is who's the person to go and actually fix this vulnerability?
zh: 企业面临的最大挑战之一是，该派谁去真正修复这个漏洞？

speaker: Unknown
en: For that, we have agents that will not only look at spreadsheets and configuration management databases in a place like ServiceNow, but also will trawl through documentation and logs and tickets and all these sources of tribal knowledge and enterprise insights, piece that together and come up with the right answer.
zh: 为此，我们的智能体不仅会查看电子表格和像 ServiceNow 这样的配置管理数据库，还会翻查文档、日志、工单以及所有这些隐性知识和企业洞察的来源，把这些拼在一起，得出正确的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think more philosophically, the approach that we're taking
zh: 所以我认为从更哲学的角度来说，我们采取的方法

speaker: Unknown
en: Is for an organization that's properly staffed with adequate resourcing and the right skill of those resources, what would a human do?
zh: 是，对于一个人员配置充足、资源到位且这些资源具备合适技能的组织，一个人类会怎么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: And as much as possible, shift a lot of those components over to the machine and let humans focus on the most complex creative and strategic work.
zh: 然后尽可能地把这些组成部分中的大部分转移给机器，让人类专注于最复杂的创造性和战略性工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing that's pretty cool about AI agents is it allows us to solve this category of problems that were not solvable in the past.
zh: AI 智能体另一件很酷的事情是，它让我们能够解决过去无法解决的一类问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we all know AI agents have superhuman context, superhuman reasoning, superhuman response time, but they're also very cheap.
zh: 我们都知道 AI 智能体拥有超人类的上下文、超人类的推理能力、超人类的响应时间，但它们还非常便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's other use case in cybersecurity that we all could imagine being done in the past, but they were
zh: 所以网络安全领域还有一些其他用例，我们过去都能想象可以做，但它们

speaker: Unknown
en: Impractically costly, right?
zh: 成本高得不切实际，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I know there's a bunch in the vulnerability management space.
zh: 我知道漏洞管理领域有一堆这样的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: In email security, think about phishing training.
zh: 在电子邮件安全方面，想想网络钓鱼训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's many CISOs over time that said, hey, can we just send out a personalized attack, right, to every single person based on the real attacks, their job and their role and everything they've done, right?
zh: 这些年来有很多 CISO 说过，嘿，我们能不能基于真实的攻击、对方的职位和角色以及他们做过的一切，给每一个人发送一次个性化的攻击，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is that might require like an army of security interns, security analysts to go do that.
zh: 问题是那可能需要一大批安全实习生、安全分析师去做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we can have an AI agent go through every single person's history, look at all the real attacks they have, make sure every person gets personalized training.
zh: 现在我们可以让一个 AI 智能体去翻查每个人的历史记录，查看他们遇到过的所有真实攻击，确保每个人都得到个性化的训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is why we're in a really exciting time with AI agents where there's things that were theoretically possible in the past but not practical.
zh: 所以这就是为什么我们正处于 AI 智能体一个非常激动人心的时刻，过去有些事情在理论上可行但不切实际。

speaker: Unknown
en: And AI agents now allow these things that used to be science fiction to become reality.
zh: 而 AI 智能体现在让那些曾经属于科幻的事情变成了现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so are there any good examples of use cases for agents that customers have pulled you in or asked you about that like you just said might have been science fiction a while ago but now that's a direction that you're exploring that you might have not been thinking about before?
zh: 那么有没有什么好的智能体用例例子，是客户主动找你或向你询问的，就像你刚才说的，可能在不久之前还属于科幻，但现在成为了你们正在探索的方向，而你们之前可能没有想过？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think the one that comes top of mind is probably identity threat detection response and insider risk.
zh: 我觉得最先想到的可能是身份威胁检测响应和内部人员风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the challenge that a lot of customers face is they have a bunch of identities in the organization.
zh: 我认为很多客户面临的挑战是，他们组织里有一大堆身份。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the past it was mostly human identities, but now it can be non-human identities or even AI agents themselves.
zh: 过去 mostly 是人类身份，但现在可以是非人类身份，甚至可以是 AI 智能体本身。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at some point, you know, these identities can be compromised, right?
zh: 而在某个时刻，你知道的，这些身份可能会被攻陷，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: An external party, usually a bad guy can come take over that identity.
zh: 一个外部方，通常是坏人，可以过来接管那个身份。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or it could be like a rogue insider, right?
zh: 或者也可能是一个变节的内部人员，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you have a spy inside your company, which sounds a little bit, you know, far-fetched, but unfortunately it happens.
zh: 也许你的公司内部有一个间谍，这听起来有点，你知道的，牵强，但不幸的是这种事确实会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it happens all the time.
zh: 是的，这种事一直在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you identify, right, that someone is doing something bad?
zh: 那么如何识别，对吧，某个人正在做坏事？

speaker: Unknown
en: In the past, you might have to have a whole team that's watching every click and every keystroke, going through every log of what that person or that identity does.
zh: 过去，你可能需要一整个团队盯着每一次点击、每一次按键，翻阅那个人或那个身份所做的每一个日志。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now you can have an AI agent do that.
zh: 但现在你可以让一个 AI 智能体来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where it's actually looking for different, you know, creating models of baseline behavior, looking for anomalies.
zh: 它实际上是在寻找不同的，你知道的，建立基线行为的模型，寻找异常。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it sees something, maybe it escalates to a human, or maybe it's so blatantly obvious it can take an action, kick that person out of their account, reset passwords, block access, create a behavioral kind of case report about what was suspicious.
zh: 如果它发现了什么，也许它会升级给人类，或者也许情况非常明显，它可以直接采取行动，把那个人踢出账户、重置密码、封锁访问、创建一份关于可疑行为的报告。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think there's like new capabilities that we're going to create that allow for better, you know, threat detection response for both, you know, compromised identities as well as kind of malicious insiders that I think if you told a CISO from that 10 years ago this would be possible, it would sound very science fictiony and I think that's like very close to reality today.
zh: 所以我认为我们将创造出一些新能力，能够对被入侵的身份以及恶意内部人员实现更好的威胁检测响应，我认为如果你在十年前告诉一位 CISO 这是可能的，那听起来会非常科幻，而我认为这在今天已经非常接近现实了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vineet?
zh: Vineet？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the best example I can think of of something that would have been perceived as science fiction five years ago but is slowly becoming more and more possible is actually autonomous remediation.
zh: 我能想到的最好的例子，一件五年前会被视为科幻、但现在正慢慢变得越来越可能的事情，实际上就是自主修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have a vulnerability and you invoke a patch or some other type of mitigation to go and diffuse that vulnerability.
zh: 也就是说你有一个漏洞，然后你调用一个补丁或其他类型的缓解措施去消除那个漏洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the challenge, and I think part of the reason why cybersecurity is one of the most interesting areas of applied AI is that you have to be right.
zh: 而挑战在于——我认为这也是网络安全成为应用 AI 最有趣的领域之一的部分原因——你必须是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if you make a mistake in one direction, the company could get breached, which is why we were hired in the first place.
zh: 因为如果你朝一个方向犯错，公司可能被攻破，而这正是当初雇用我们的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the other direction, maybe you push a bad patch, you take down a system, and the company loses millions of dollars of revenue, right?
zh: 而朝另一个方向，也许你推送了一个糟糕的补丁，搞垮了一个系统，公司损失数百万美元的收入，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So especially for enterprise companies, there's been a lot of hesitance in terms of automation and vulnerability management, and especially kind of turning over the remediation lifecycle to a machine.
zh: 所以尤其是对企业公司来说，在自动化和漏洞管理方面一直有很多犹豫，尤其是把修复生命周期交给机器这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think people are realizing that as you take a five-year view, when you're being attacked by a machine, you can't sit around waiting for change control.
zh: 但我认为人们正在意识到，从五年的视角来看，当你被机器攻击时，你不能坐在那里等变更控制流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've had some of the stodgiest, most legacy types of companies now come to us and say, hey, Cogent, what are you doing on autonomous remediation?
zh: 所以现在连一些最古板、最传统类型的公司也来找我们说，嘿，Cogent，你们在自主修复方面做了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you just take this problem off our hands and do it at machine speed?
zh: 你能直接把这个 problem 从我们手上接过去，以机器速度完成吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there is a journey there.
zh: 所以这中间有一段旅程。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot more work to do to get the level of integrity and accuracy that companies require.
zh: 要达到公司所要求的完整性和准确性水平，还有很多工作要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's not science fiction.
zh: 但这不是科幻。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's here today.
zh: 它今天就在这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's something that we're going to continue delivering.
zh: 而且这是我们会持续交付的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a great example.
zh: 这是个很好的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one thing that you just said, Vinita, I want to pick on.
zh: 还有刚才你说的其中一件事，Vinita，我想追问一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what makes a customer ready to adopt agentic security?
zh: 那么是什么让客户准备好采用智能体化的安全？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there any rules of thumb on environments or just preparedness that they might have to work with someone like Cogent?
zh: 在环境方面，或者在他们必须与像 Cogent 这样的公司合作之前的准备程度方面，有什么经验法则吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So the good thing about the problem we're tackling, it's a big and wide problem, and there's something for everyone.
zh: 我们正在 tackling 的这个问题有个好处，它是一个又大又宽的问题，每个人都能从中找到适合自己的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see that there's a lot of manual operational work that happens in vulnerability management, whether it's gathering context on an asset, looking at threat intelligence of who's exploiting a vulnerability.
zh: 我们看到在漏洞管理中有很多手动的操作工作，无论是收集某个资产的相关信息，还是查看谁在利用某个漏洞的威胁情报。

speaker: Unknown
en: Virtually 100% of folks that we talk to want that fully automated.
zh: 几乎 100% 与我们交谈过的人都希望这部分完全自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't want to think about it.
zh: 他们不想去操心它。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just want some package of information that is collected by an AI agent and passed on to a human.
zh: 他们只想要一包由 AI 智能体收集并传递给人类的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I think where there's some segmentation in the market is for teams that are very lean, maybe they don't even have anybody that's devoted full-time to cybersecurity, especially if we see this in kind of startups and smaller companies, they just want full autonomy, right?
zh: 现在市场的分层在于，对于非常精简的团队，也许他们甚至没有任何全职投入网络安全的人，尤其是我们在初创公司和小公司中看到的这种情况，他们只想要完全的自主，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: They say go and, you know, do whatever you want, cogent, right?
zh: 他们说，去吧，随便你怎么做，Cogent，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you make a mistake, that's fine because we're going to be no better as humans.
zh: 如果你犯了错，没关系，因为作为人类我们也不会做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, in bigger enterprises where, you know, they have bigger teams and the consequences of making a mistake can be catastrophic for their brand, for their revenue.
zh: 而在更大的企业中，他们有更大的团队，犯错的后果对他们的品牌、收入可能是灾难性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They kind of prefer a mode where it's more assistive, right?
zh: 他们更倾向于一种更具辅助性的模式，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Coach and do all the analysis and empower a human to make better decisions, but still have a human as a validator for the purpose of accountability.
zh: 做所有分析并赋能人类做出更好的决策，但为了问责的目的，仍然让人类作为验证者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the reality is, you know, as we scale over time, it's not going to be a zero to one inflection.
zh: 我认为现实是，随着我们随时间扩大规模，这不会是一次从零到一的转折点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be gradual slices of work that shift towards automation.
zh: 而会是逐渐一块一块的工作向自动化转移。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so some of these enterprises are eventually going to be comfortable and they're going to say, for my laptops or for my dev environment, go run autonomy end to end.
zh: 所以这些企业中的一些最终会变得放心，他们会说，对于我的笔记本电脑或我的开发环境，端到端地运行自主系统吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for my most mission critical production servers, I still want a human in the loop.
zh: 而对于我最关键任务的生产服务器，我仍然想要人在回路中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for us, our goal is to meet these customers where they are, still give them significant leverage and uplift, but give them optionality in terms of the point and the curve that they want to pick.
zh: 所以对我们来说，我们的目标是在客户所在的地方满足他们，仍然给他们显著的杠杆和提升，但在他们想选择的曲线上的那个点给他们可选性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, Evan, you just described an incredible example that kind of feels like science fiction.
zh: 还有，是的，Evan，你刚才描述了一个让人觉得像科幻的惊人例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are enterprises well-positioned to adopt a technology that kind of can do that level of automation that you just described?
zh: 那么企业是否有足够的条件去采用一种能够实现你刚才描述的那种自动化水平的技术？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think objectively and empirically, yes.
zh: 我认为客观且凭经验来看，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have, again, more than one out of four, maybe one out of five, four to five of our companies already deploying that production today.
zh: 我们再一次看到，四分之一以上，也许五分之一，我们四到五家公司今天已经在生产环境中部署了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a couple of prerequisites, right?
zh: 有几个先决条件，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you have to be cloud forward, right, because these things run in the cloud.
zh: 你必须拥抱云，对吧，因为这些东西运行在云中。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to also be willing to accept that the AI can make smarter decisions than at least some of your humans some of the time.
zh: 你还必须愿意接受 AI 至少在某些时候能比你的某些人类做出更聪明的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it has to be kind of some level of trust that AI is going to do what it's supposed to do.
zh: 所以必须有一定程度的信任，相信 AI 会去做它应该做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we look at customers that kind of come to us.
zh: 你看，来找我们的那些客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's for probably one of three reasons.
zh: 这大概是出于三个原因之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is just like fed up with like email being at the top of the list, like the biggest risk, the biggest cause of risk, the biggest cause of financial loss.
zh: 一是实在受够了电子邮件排在风险清单的最上面，是最大的风险、最大的风险成因、最大的财务损失来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's probably the most common one.
zh: 这可能是最常见的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second one is, you know, I imagine it's similar for you, Vinny.
zh: 第二个原因，你知道的，Vinny，我想对你来说也是类似的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, people are just trying to like save time and energy, right?
zh: 就是，人们只是想节省时间和精力，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone's talking about
zh: （更正）[[224]] 我觉得我们这个领域的一个类比就是，比如，钓鱼演练培训。

speaker: Unknown
en: The magic of AI and automation.
zh: AI 和自动化的魔力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think a lot of people are really getting the productivity gains they'd expect out of the SOC.
zh: 我不认为很多人真的从 SOC 中获得了他们所期望的生产力提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: So sometimes people are just like, okay, like we need the computers to do like some of the work for the machines, right?
zh: 所以有时候人们就是觉得，好吧，我们需要计算机帮机器做一些工作，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that the third reason is people also just trying to get ready for the future, right?
zh: 而我认为第三个原因是，人们也只是想为未来做好准备，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we all know that AI will play a big role in cybersecurity.
zh: 我想我们都知道，AI 将在网络安全中扮演重要角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think a lot of, you know, kind of forward-leaning CISOs want to at least kind of invest in some of these, right, to like pave the way for future options.
zh: 所以我想很多，你知道，比较超前的 CISO 至少想投资其中一些，对吧，为未来的选择铺路。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or sometimes just try to be a leader inside the company and say, hey, we're going to deliver a very clear use case where AI is giving us, you know, risk reduction and productivity wins and maybe saving us money at the same time, right?
zh: 或者有时候只是想在公司内部做一个领导者，说，嘿，我们将交付一个非常明确的使用案例，AI 在其中为我们带来风险降低和生产力收益，也许同时还为我们省钱，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of a win-win-win.
zh: 有点像三赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe one point I'll add on top of that is people oftentimes think of these departments like cybersecurity in isolation, right?
zh: 也许我要补充的一点是，人们 oftentimes 把这些部门，比如网络安全，孤立地看待，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So make cyber teams more effective and more efficient.
zh: 也就是让网络安全团队更有效、更高效。

speaker: Unknown
en: What they don't think about is the second order consequences.
zh: 而他们没有考虑的是二阶后果。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in our case, right, vulnerability management, security is accountable for risk, but ultimately engineers and IT folks are the ones doing the work to actually fix them.
zh: 以我们的情况为例，对吧，漏洞管理，安全部门对风险负有责任，但最终是工程师和 IT 人员在实际做修复工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've talked to organizations, tech companies, banks, Fortune 500s, where they've actually sized this and they spend millions of dollars of resourcing within engineering teams just fixing the vulnerabilities.
zh: 所以我们和不少组织谈过，科技公司、银行、财富 500 强，他们真的测算过，他们在工程团队内部花费了数百万美元的资源，仅仅用于修复漏洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you were to reclaim that and now allocate that towards revenue driving initiatives, building new products, the impact your business could be enormous.
zh: 所以如果你能把这些回收回来，重新分配给推动营收的举措、构建新产品，那对你业务的影响可能是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, in kind of your example, like, you know, you could save maybe the SOC a couple hours, right?
zh: 是的，我是说，拿你的例子来说，你知道，你可能可以给 SOC 节省几个小时，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But what if you could save everyone in the technology team an hour a month?
zh: 但如果你能给整个技术团队的每个人每月节省一个小时呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: They have an extra hour free.
zh: 他们多出了一个小时的空闲时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: What if they're putting that towards the productivity-increasing products and revenue-generating products, right?
zh: 如果他们把这段时间投入到提高生产力的产品和创收的产品上呢，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that the analogy behind our world is, like, phishing training.
zh: 我觉得我们这个领域的一个类比就是，比如，钓鱼演练培训。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, everyone in the company spent hours to do phishing training that's, like, generic and it's very time-consuming.

zh: AI 是否实实在在地改变了你们团队的工作方式？

speaker: Unknown
en: And describe to us how.
zh: 请向我们描述是如何改变的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say undeniably, yes.
zh: 我会说，毫无疑问，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even when Vineet and I were working together at Abnormal, right, we saw some of these changes coming, but probably also...
zh: 即使在 Vineet 和我一起在 Abnormal 工作的时候，对吧，我们就看到了这些变化中的一些正在到来，但可能也……

speaker: Unknown
en: Underestimated like how fast they would come and how impactful they would be.
zh: 低估了它们会来得有多快、影响会有多大。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way we think about abnormal is we're trying to do less about what can we do tomorrow is a little bit better than yesterday.
zh: 我们对 Abnormal 的思考方式是，我们不太关注明天能比昨天做得好一点点什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead we're trying to do is think about how should an AI native company work two or three years in the future?
zh: 相反，我们试图做的是思考，一家 AI 原生公司在两三年后应该如何运作？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that look like?
zh: 那会是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then how do we kind of work backwards from that?
zh: 然后我们如何从那个未来倒推回来？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the big difference between kind of the work forward versus work backwards is, you know, are humans initiating the AI or is AI initiating kind of the humans, right?
zh: 我认为正向工作与倒推工作之间的重大区别是，是人类在启动 AI，还是 AI 在启动人类，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so today a lot of kind of conventional AI usage is you're prompting some large language model to get some feedback back.
zh: 所以今天，很多传统的 AI 使用方式是，你给某个大语言模型写提示词，以获得一些反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, in the future, the way an AI-native company needs to work is that AI is kind of doing some initiation.
zh: 我认为，在未来，一家 AI 原生公司的运作方式应该是，由 AI 来做某种发起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what does a software company do, right, an enterprise software?
zh: 比如，一家软件公司是做什么的，对吧，企业软件？

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, listen to customers, figure out what they want, and, like, build some code, and then give it back, and then kind of give it back to them, right?
zh: 基本上，倾听客户，弄清楚他们想要什么，然后构建一些代码，然后交回去，再把东西交还给他们，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So just that kind of life cycle has totally changed.
zh: 所以仅仅是这样一个生命周期就已经完全改变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the past, you know, I would go talk to 20 customers a week, which is a very small percentage of our customers.
zh: 在过去，你知道，我一周会去和 20 个客户交谈，这只占我们客户中很小的比例。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would understand some of it, communicate some of that, and probably make some of those changes.
zh: 我会理解其中一部分，传达其中一部分，并且可能做出其中一些改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of our goals is to make sure that, like, every time we cut feedback from customers, that gets to our code base in 24 hours.
zh: 所以我们的目标之一是确保，每当我们收到来自客户的反馈，它都能在 24 小时内进入我们的代码库。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Every single word.
zh: 每一个字。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how does that change how it worked today?
zh: 那这如何改变它今天的运作方式呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you know, for, I don't know, 50% of our calls to customers where we're getting feedback, it was recorded.
zh: 嗯,你知道,大概有 50% 的客户通话——我们收集反馈的那些——是被录制下来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have deep research agents that go through all that and they find all the patterns.
zh: 我们有深度研究智能体去遍历所有这些内容,它们会找出所有的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every week a product manager at Abnormal will get an email from kind of basic AI saying, here's the top bugs, here's top features, here's the customers don't understand, here's where our Salesforce doesn't understand, right?
zh: 每周,Abnormal 的产品经理都会收到一封来自基础 AI 的邮件,上面写着:这是最严重的 bug,这是最热门的功能需求,这是客户不理解的地方,这是我们的销售团队不理解的地方,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: They then kind of take that.
zh: 然后他们会拿走这些内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some judgment applied by that kind of product person.
zh: 那位产品人员会做一些判断。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have these generated kind of micro PRDs for those product features.
zh: 我们会为这些产品功能生成一些微型 PRD。

speaker: Unknown
en: We use AI to do technology selection, like what JavaScript library should implement that animation on the menu.
zh: 我们用 AI 来做技术选型,比如菜单上那个动画该用哪个 JavaScript 库来实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: That all goes into, like, obviously, AI-generated code.
zh: 这些全都汇入 AI 生成的代码里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we see kind of that whole process from kind of customer feedback to, like, generating code.
zh: 所以我们看到的,是从客户反馈到生成代码的整个流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's, you know, obviously, that gets revolutionized with AI, helping us supercharge our sales force so we can be more personalized and relevant to every customer interaction, and just improving our operations and productivity across the enterprise.
zh: 显然,这一切都被 AI 革命化了,它帮助我们为销售团队赋能,让我们在每一次客户互动中都能更个性化、更切中需求,同时提升整个企业的运营和生产力。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's incredible.
zh: 真是不可思议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vineet?
zh: Vineet?

speaker: Unknown
en: Work in progress.
zh: 还在进行中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, work in progress.
zh: 是啊,还在进行中。

speaker: Unknown
en: How have you adopted AI as you're building Cogent?
zh: 你在打造 Cogent 的过程中是如何采用 AI 的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think, first of all, just building in the age of AI is super exciting.
zh: 嗯,我认为,首先,在 AI 时代创业是非常令人兴奋的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we have a lot of folks on our team that have spent decades in industry, and they unanimously say that this is the most exciting time that they've been alive, right, and working on things, because they're much more efficient, much more productive.
zh: 我认为我们团队里有很多人在行业内干了几十年,他们一致表示,这是他们有生以来最兴奋的时期,对吧,也是他们从事工作时最兴奋的时期,因为他们效率更高、生产力更强。

speaker: Unknown
en: The benefit of being a younger company is that we've had the opportunity to actually build AI from the ground up and incorporate it into the fabric of all of our core processes.
zh: 作为一家较年轻的公司的优势在于,我们有机会从一开始就把 AI 融入进来,把它纳入所有核心流程的组织结构之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think two interesting developments of all that that would have completely surprised me a couple years ago.
zh: 我认为这当中有两个有意思的进展,要是几年前会让我完全意想不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: Number one, everybody's become a builder.
zh: 第一,每个人都成了构建者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've had members of the go-to-market team where by all measures they should not be able to write code and these guys are building applications and tools to go and solve the problems that they have.
zh: 我见过市场销售(go-to-market)团队的成员,按各种标准衡量他们都不该会写代码,但这些人正在构建应用程序和工具,去解决他们自己遇到的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's been this democratization of people who can solve problems and use software to go and make their lives better.
zh: 我认为这实现了一种普及化:更多人能够解决问题,并用软件让自己的生活变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think second is just an accentuation of the human touch.
zh: 而我认为第二点是人际温度的凸显。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as we have AI agents cranking pull requests in the background, we'll have five engineers on the whiteboard and animated discussions about what to build and how to build it.
zh: 所以,当我们的 AI 智能体在后台批量产出 pull request 时,会有五位工程师站在白板前,热烈讨论要构建什么以及怎么构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we'll have sales folks that are out with customers building relationships and talking about their personal lives.
zh: 我们的销售人员则会和客户在外接触,建立关系,聊他们的私人生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are things that AI is not well suited for and the human is still the king for.
zh: 这些是 AI 不擅长的事情,而且人类在这些方面仍然是王者。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's been interesting as well.
zh: 所以这一点也很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the age of AI, some of these human types of interactions and skill sets become that much more valuable.
zh: 在 AI 时代,某些人类类型的互动和技能变得更加有价值了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's cool because like it allows really every employee to also increase the level of abstraction they're working at and I think you know probably the average employee today compared to six months ago right certainly a little bit abnormal probably very true for your company just because like you said you're starting almost from scratch right it allows all of us workers higher leverage things and do less boring things.
zh: 这很酷,因为它让每一位员工都能提高自己工作的抽象层级,而且我认为,你知道,今天的普通员工和六个月前相比,对吧——对 Abnormal 来说当然更是如此,对你公司来说可能也很适用,因为就像你说的,你们几乎是从零开始的,对吧——它让我们所有工作者都能做更高杠杆的事情,少做枯燥的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I want to actually touch on the team and talent for a minute.
zh: 我想实际聊一下团队和人才。

speaker: Unknown
en: Evan, you've clearly built an extremely entrepreneurial culture of talent at Abnormal and really kept that going over the years.
zh: Evan,你显然在 Abnormal 打造了一个极具创业精神的人才文化,并且这些年一直保持了下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell us a little bit about how you think about team building and culture at Abnormal.
zh: 跟我们讲讲你是如何看待 Abnormal 的团队建设和文化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I mean, everyone's got a different definition of culture.
zh: 嗯,我是说,每个人对文化的定义都不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: My kind of definition is culture's kind of the sum of all the behaviors across the enterprise that express some underlying core set of values.
zh: 我的定义大概是:文化是企业内所有行为的总和,这些行为表达了某种底层的核心价值观。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for us, like our number one thing is be long-term oriented, right?
zh: 对我们来说,比如我们的头号信条是保持长期主义,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: If you, you know, I started the company to be a generational company.
zh: 如果——你知道,我创办这家公司就是想做成一家跨越世代的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to be a generational company as a business,
zh: 如果你想要作为一家企业成为跨越世代的公司,

speaker: Unknown
en: The next core value is like be very customer-oriented, right?
zh: 下一个核心价值观是高度以客户为导向,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Your customers have to get a lot of value, perceive the value, and pay you if you want to be around for a while.
zh: 你的客户必须获得大量价值、感知到这份价值,并为此付费,你才能长久存续。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I won't go through all of our core values while I want to.
zh: 所以虽然我想,但我不会把我们所有核心价值观都讲一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our five core values are all derived from that.
zh: 我们的五个核心价值观都由此推导而来。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the values that inspire behaviors that our customers value?
zh: 哪些价值观能激发我们的客户所看重的行为?

speaker: Unknown
en: We want people to come for the mission because they want to stop some crime, put some bad guys in jail.
zh: 我们希望人们为使命而来,因为他们想阻止一些犯罪,把一些坏人送进监狱。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want people to want to work on the cutting edge of AI, whether it's in the product or kind of selling the product or helping support those things.
zh: 我们希望人们愿意在 AI 的最前沿工作,无论是做产品,还是销售产品,或是帮助支持这些工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the third one is like people who want to actually improve their craft, right?
zh: 第三点是,人们想要真正提升自己的技艺,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And Vinny, you know, Vinny found all buckets, right?
zh: 而 Vinny,你知道,Vinny 占全了所有类型,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But the third one, it was like, Vinny's like, I want to be a great AI native CEO, AI native founder.
zh: 至于第三点,就像 Vinny 说的:我想成为一名伟大的 AI 原生 CEO、AI 原生创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to build great products that are customer oriented that solve real problems in the world.
zh: 我想打造出色的、以客户为导向的产品，去解决世界上真实存在的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my hope is that it's not, you know, well, Vineet was a net loss, right, to the company, obviously.
zh: 我希望事情不会变成，你知道的，好吧，Vineet 对公司来说显然是一笔净损失，对吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's probably five other people out there that want to be the next Vineet.
zh: 外面大概还有另外五个人想成为下一个 Vineet。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, yeah, some people are going to leave, but if we really invest in our employees, that will kind of all work out in the long run.
zh: 所以，是的，有些人会离开，但如果我们真正投资于员工，长远来看这一切都会好起来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what was your reaction when he told you that he wanted to start his own company?
zh: 那当他告诉你他想创办自己的公司时，你的反应是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably what I said, or hopefully what I said, at least I don't want to remember in my head.
zh: 我说的那些话吧，或者希望是我说的那些话，至少我不想记在心里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think my advice was like, you got to find a place that is going to best prepare you for that.
zh: 我记得我的建议是，你得找一个最能为此做好准备的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great companies take, you know, as you know, probably better than most, they take 10 years, 20 years, 30 years.
zh: 伟大的公司，你知道的，你大概比大多数人都清楚，它们需要 10 年、20 年、30 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're going to spend 20 years to go on like a really worthy pursuit.
zh: 所以你要花 20 年去追求一件真正值得的事业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go take the first two or three years and really prepare.
zh: 那就把头两三年拿出来，真正做好准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: Build the skills, build the network, build the relationships, build up the culture and values that can help you on the next 17 years.
zh: 打造技能、打造人脉、打造关系、打造文化和价值观，让它们在你接下来的 17 年里帮到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is exactly what Vinny did and I would highly recommend it for anyone who wants to be an entrepreneur.
zh: Vinny 做的正是这件事，我强烈推荐给任何想成为创业者的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go to a place where you can really learn, where you're surrounded by very talented people in a culture that is customer-oriented, innovation-focused, and just learn as much as possible.
zh: 去一个你真正能学习的地方，那里有非常有才华的人围绕着你，有一种以客户为导向、以创新为核心的文化，然后尽可能多地学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you find the right spot, you can get a decade of career experience in a year or two.
zh: 如果你找到了对的地方，你可以在一两年的时间里获得十年的职业经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And really use that to kind of get paid to prepare for your own journey.
zh: 并且真正利用它，算是拿工资为自己未来的旅程做准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: One more thing I'd add, and I think it's really important for any early career talent to assess as they evaluate companies, is being in an ecosystem where there's an active commitment to nurturing that talent and developing them.
zh: 我还想补充一点，我认为对任何早期职业人才在评估公司时都非常重要的一点是，身处一个对培养和发展人才有积极承诺的生态系统中。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember being early on, and I had this vague notion that starting a company could be cool.
zh: 我记得我很早的时候，有一种模糊的想法，觉得创办公司可能会很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many of my role models had gotten on that path, but I had no idea how to get there.
zh: 我的许多榜样都走上了那条路，但我完全不知道怎么到达那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even in the early days, Evan would take hours and hours of his personal time.
zh: 甚至在早期，Evan 会拿出他个人时间中大量的几个小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'd be meeting at midnight Eastern, going through OKRs and potential individual career plans for the future.
zh: 我们会在东部时间午夜开会，过 OKR 和未来潜在的个人职业规划。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very rare to have leadership that's willing to allocate that type of time to people who are not executives at a company, but maybe, you know, at the bottom of the organization, but they see that potential and they're willing to invest.
zh: 很少有领导层愿意把这种类型的时间分配给那些在公司里不是高管、也许处于组织底层的人，但他们看到了那种潜力，并且愿意投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was very foundational for my, you know, career growth and success.
zh: 这对我的职业成长和成功来说是非常根基性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I just remember within a couple months of meeting Vineet, I had some sense that he would be, I was like, how about this kind of boss of the future, so I better, like, invest now.
zh: 你知道，我只记得在认识 Vineet 后的几个月内，我就有某种感觉他会成为，我当时想，这可是未来某种老板，所以我最好现在就投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: We certainly had that feeling as well.
zh: 我们当时也确实有那种感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think like, especially in small startups, there's great opportunities for people to take a lot of ownership and agency and kind of help drive their career forward.
zh: 但我认为，尤其是在小型初创公司里，有很多机会让人们承担大量责任和主观能动性，从而推动自己的职业前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Vinit would take up more ownership, he'd probably get exposed to new things and learn more.
zh: 所以 Vinit 会承担更多责任，他可能会接触到新事物并学到更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think even though we knew, we both knew at some point Vinit was going to leave and go start his own company, but it was still a very, you know, it was a really great relationship.
zh: 而且我觉得，尽管我们知道，我们俩都知道 Vinit 迟早会离开去创办自己的公司，但这仍然是一段非常、你知道的、非常棒的关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vinit, is there a habit or a trait that you saw in Evan as a CEO that you want to replicate as the CEO of Cogent?
zh: Vinit，你在 Evan 身上作为 CEO 看到了什么习惯或特质，是你作为 Cogent 的 CEO 想要复刻的？

speaker: Unknown
en: How much time do we have left?
zh: 我们还剩多少时间？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sorry.
zh: 抱歉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have all the time in the world.
zh: 我有全世界所有的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if you can go through the full list.
zh: 我不确定你能不能把完整的清单都过一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a characteristic that Evan possesses that I've also seen in other great leaders that have gotten the chance to meet over time is just attention to detail, right?
zh: 我认为 Evan 拥有的一种特质，我在这些年有机会见到的其他伟大领导者身上也见过，那就是对细节的关注，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you oftentimes hear that best practice is work yourself out of a job, you know, elevate.
zh: 我想你经常听到所谓的最佳实践是把自己从工作中解放出来，你知道的，去提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can be on the beach while the company's running.
zh: 你可以躺在海滩上，而公司照常运转。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I've worked on projects with Evan where it's like, you know, 26 page Google documents, every single bullet point carefully crafted.
zh: 你知道，我和 Evan 一起做项目时，会有 26 页的 Google 文档，每一个要点都是精心打磨的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Evan kind of understands the details and he could go roll up his sleeves and do any job at the company and that's not beneath him.
zh: Evan 真正理解那些细节，他可以挽起袖子去做公司里的任何工作，那对他来说并不掉价。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that's kind of a mentality that I've tried to embody as well.
zh: 所以我认为这也是一种我努力去体现的心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's also causal for abnormal success because oftentimes a lot of the early decisions you make in a company that seem small and insignificant
zh: 我认为这也非常导致超常的成功，因为很多时候你在公司早期做的很多决定看似微小且无关紧要

speaker: Unknown
en: Having better paths that you go down there can compound into tremendous advantage over time.
zh: 在那些地方走上更好的路径，随着时间推移可以复利成巨大的优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one thing that was actually very impactful for me as well, I had this idea around, I think, the 2022 timeframe.
zh: 还有一件事实际上对我也影响很大，大概在 2022 年前后我有了这个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, I'm soaking up so much from Abrormal, learning from people like Evan, other executives at the company.
zh: 我当时想，我从 Abnormal 吸收了这么多东西，向 Evan 这样的人、公司的其他高管学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: In five years, I'm going to forget all of this, and it's going to be all for naught.
zh: 五年后，我会把这些全忘掉，那这一切就都白费了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I started basically creating this journal.
zh: 所以我基本上开始创建这本日志。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, it's a Google document in my personal Google Drive.
zh: 实际上，它是我个人 Google Drive 里的一个 Google 文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: No IP in there.
zh: 里面没有任何知识产权。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's called the Abnormal Playbook.
zh: 但它叫 Abnormal Playbook。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was just like, every time I learned something, I'd write it down there.
zh: 我就是每次学到什么东西，就把它记在那里面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the time I left in 2024, it'd become this 80-page manual of just how to build and operate a company.
zh: 到我 2024 年离开的时候，它已经变成了一本 80 页的手册，全是关于如何建设和运营一家公司的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, of course, there's certain things that are changing in the ecosystem.
zh: 所以，当然，生态系统中有些东西正在变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not the perfect thing to go and replicate everything Abnormal did seven years ago.
zh: 把 Abnormal 七年前做的一切都照搬复制，并不是完美的做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But 75% of that still applies.
zh: 但其中 75% 仍然适用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I actually think that that's been a massive catalyst for us in our journey, where myself, I'm a first-time founder, but in some capacities, I feel like a second-time founder.
zh: 而且我真的认为，这在我们各自的旅程中是一个巨大的催化剂——我自己是首次创业者，但在某种程度上，我感觉自己像是二次创业者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen it before, right?
zh: 我以前见过这些，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of that is due to the things that I learned at Abnormal.
zh: 而这在很大程度上要归功于我在 Abnormal 学到的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you talk a little bit about your learnings from your time at Abnormal and really what have you brought over to Cogent?
zh: 你能谈谈你在 Abnormal 工作期间的收获吗，以及你真正把什么带到了 Cogent?

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot that we've brought over.
zh: 我们带过来了很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I kind of view abnormal as, first of all...
zh: 而我有点把 Abnormal 看作是，首先……

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing illegally brought over.
zh: 没有任何非法带过来的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Conceptually.
zh: 是概念上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything above board.
zh: 一切都光明正大。

speaker: Unknown
en: But abnormal was, quite frankly, the most rewarding experience in both my professional and personal life.
zh: 但说实话，Abnormal 是我职业生涯和个人生活中最有收获的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think what was really great there, and this is the advice I give to all the candidates that are evaluating Cogent and other companies as well,
zh: 我觉得那里真正好的一点，这也是我给所有正在评估 Cogent 和其他公司的候选人提的建议，

speaker: Unknown
en: First of all, you want to join a rocket ship, right?
zh: 首先，你要加入一艘火箭，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one thing that was a boon to myself and all of my colleagues at Abnormal is that we just witnessed incredible growth, right?
zh: 我认为对我自己和我在 Abnormal 的所有同事来说有一大幸事，就是我们亲眼见证了不可思议的增长，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And when, you know, your company's scaling, when there's new problems to be solved, there's kind of no choice but to take the people that you have on board and elevate them, right, and give them more things to do.
zh: 当你的公司在扩张，当有新问题需要解决时，你基本上别无选择，只能把你已有的人才提拔起来，给他们更多的事情做，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think you have to pick the company wisely and think of it the same way as an investor.
zh: 所以我认为你必须明智地挑选公司，并且像投资者一样去思考它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually the difference is that an investor has multiple shots on goal and you only have one career.
zh: 而实际上区别在于，投资者有多次射门机会，而你只有一次职业生涯。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the difference between selecting the right opportunity and a subpar opportunity, that can have orders of magnitude of impact as that compounds over time.
zh: 选对机会和选中次优机会之间的差别，随着时间复利累积，可能产生数量级级别的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the pieces that ties into that is the strength of the leadership.
zh: 与此相关的一个要素是领导层的实力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go on.
zh: 继续。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the part that Evan paid before.
zh: 这是 Evan 之前付钱的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sponsored by.
zh: 赞助的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The charisma, the thoughtfulness, the humility.
zh: 那种魅力、那种深思熟虑、那种谦逊。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that's important, right?
zh: 但我认为这很重要，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: There's many startups that are out there, especially in this era where there's a lot of noise in the ecosystem.
zh: 市面上有很多初创公司，尤其是在这个生态系统里充满噪音的时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the reasons that I was drawn to Abnormal is I looked at the leadership team and the people who would be my bosses.
zh: 我被 Abnormal 吸引的原因之一，是我看了领导团队和那些将成为我老板的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, if I was a big tech, these guys would be eight levels above me.
zh: 我当时想，如果在大厂，这些人会比我的职级高八级。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would never see them, right?
zh: 我根本见不到他们，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then being able to work hand-in-hand in the trenches with all these folks, it was just distillation, right?
zh: 而能够和这些人一起在战壕里并肩工作，简直就是一种萃取，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I was able to take their 30 years of experience and get it into my brain in like eight months, right?
zh: 我能够把他们的 30 年经验，在大约八个月的时间里装进我的脑子，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then also just the talent density of the team.
zh: 还有就是团队的人才密度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Abnormal just had a really strong nucleus.
zh: 我觉得 Abnormal 有一个非常强的核心。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were people that I could learn from and just develop problem-solving toolkits as I collaborated with them.
zh: 有些人我可以向他们学习，在与他们合作的过程中建立起解决问题的工具箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of the people that I've met at Abnormal are my current and future collaborators.
zh: 而且很多我在 Abnormal 认识的人，都是我现在和未来的合作者。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're fellow founders.
zh: 他们是同为创业者的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, things are still early for myself and many of my peers.
zh: 所以，你知道，对于我和我的许多同伴来说，一切都还很早期。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think Abnormal has the chance to be the PayPal mafia of enterprise software, which is super exciting.
zh: 但我认为 Abnormal 有机会成为企业软件界的 PayPal 黑帮，这非常令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or at least AI native software.
zh: 或者至少是 AI 原生软件界的。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI native software, that's right.
zh: AI 原生软件，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the other thing too, I think it's really important.
zh: 我认为另一件事，我觉得也非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You really want to find places that like will give opportunity, right?
zh: 你真的想找到那些愿意给你机会的地方，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: There's many, I just remember you in the early days, you're like, hey, I'm a engineering engineer, but like, can I start getting a little more involved with like customers?
zh: 有很多，我记得你早期的时候，你会说，嘿，我是个工程工程师，但我能不能多参与一些和客户相关的事情?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd love to just like learn more about how they think about a roadmap, right?
zh: 我很想多了解一下他们是如何思考路线图的，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: We're like, well, yeah, no one else is doing that.
zh: 我们就说，嗯，好啊，反正没有别人在做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to go help out, that'd be great, right?
zh: 如果你想去帮忙，那太好了，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Not all companies will have that opportunity where they let people kind of step up and raise your hand and say, hey, let me try that out, right?
zh: 并不是所有公司都有这样的机会，让人们能够站出来、举手说，嘿，让我试试那个吧，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are hard to find, but when you do like, you know, great opportunity.
zh: 那些很难找到，但一旦找到，你知道，就是绝佳的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, the three of us could go on for many more hours, but you have attackers to stop and customers to protect.
zh: 好了，我们三个还能继续聊上好几个小时，但你有攻击者要阻止，还有客户要保护。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we'll end it right here.
zh: 所以我们就在这里结束吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Evan, Vineet, thank you so much for joining us on ChangeAgents.
zh: Evan、Vineet，非常感谢你们来到 ChangeAgents。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for having us, Grant.
zh: 谢谢你们邀请我们，Grant。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having us.
zh: 谢谢你们的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。
